glosses: Rastro de los animales o personas al ir de un lugar a otro.
Elemento (físico o mental), información o deducción que se usa para tratar de llegar a un lado o descifrar una incógnita.
Calle de un campo aéreo, por donde los aviones carretean, aterrizan o despegan.
Calle de un campo de carreras o otro deporte, por donde los automóviles, personas, caballos, galgos, etc. corren.
Elemento de un disco o cinta de audio, que guarda la información sonora o visual.
Por extensión, cada canción, melodía, discurso u otras formas de sonido o video de los discos o cintas.

glosses: The interior bottom or surface of a house or building; the supporting surface of a room.

examples.text: The room has a wooden floor.
A great bargain also had been the excellent Axminster carpet which covered the floor; as, again, the arm-chair in which Bunting now sat forward, staring into the dull, small fire.

glosses: The bottom surface of a natural structure, entity, or space (e.g. cave, forest, ocean, desert, etc.); the ground (surface of the Earth).

examples.text: The leaves covering the forest floor provide many hiding-places for small animals.
Many sunken ships rest on the ocean floor.
The floor of a cave served the refugees as a home.
The pit floor showed where a ring of post holes had been.

glosses: The ground.

examples.text: After stepping off the bus, my wallet fell on the floor.

glosses: A structure formed of beams, girders, etc, with proper covering, which divides a building horizontally into storeys/stories.
The supporting surface or platform of a structure such as a bridge.

examples.text: Wooden planks of the old bridge's floor were nearly rotten.

glosses: A storey/story of a building.

examples.text: For years we lived on the third floor.

When Timothy and Julia hurried up the staircase to the bedroom floor, where a considerable commotion was taking place, Tim took Barry Leach with him. He had him gripped firmly by the arm, since he felt it was not safe to let him loose, and he had no immediate idea what to do with him.

glosses: In a parliament, the part of the house assigned to the members, as opposed to the viewing gallery.
The right to speak at a given time during a debate or other public event.

examples.text: Will the senator from Arizona yield the floor?
The mayor often gives a lobbyist the floor.

glosses: That part of the bottom of a vessel on each side of the keelson which is most nearly horizontal.
A horizontal, flat ore body; the rock underlying a stratified or nearly horizontal deposit.
The bottom of a pit, pothole or mine.
The largest integer less than or equal to a given number.

examples.text: The floor of 4.5 is 4.

glosses: An event performed on a floor-like carpeted surface; floor exercise
A floor-like carpeted surface for performing gymnastic movements.
A lower limit or minimum on a price or rate, a price floor. Opposite of a cap or ceiling.
A dance floor.

examples.text: She's a maniac, maniac on the floor / And she's dancing like she never danced before
Open the door, get on the floor / Everybody walk the dinosaur

Meet me on the floor tonight
Show me how to move like the water

glosses: The trading floor of a stock exchange, pit; the area in which business is conducted at a convention or exhibition.
The area of a casino where gambling occurs.

examples.text: At each table stood a young, slim, poker-faced croupier serving the punters who anxiously watched the turning of the cards. The next two floors were similar though not quite as spectacular and the stakes were lower.

glosses: The area of an establishment where food and drink are served to customers.

examples.text: The conference started as an impromptu session in the coffee shop this morning when waitresses walked off the floor rather than serve four Negro men and women delegates.

glosses: To cover or furnish with a floor.

examples.text: floor a house with pine boards

The huge square box, parquet-floored and high-ceilinged, had been arranged to display a suite of bedroom furniture designed and made in the halcyon days of the last quarter of the nineteenth century,[…].

glosses: To strike down or lay level with the floor; to knock down.

examples.text: Sam floored him perpetually, and beat his face to a jelly, without getting a scratch.

glosses: To hang (a picture on exhibition) near the base of a wall, where it cannot easily be seen.
To push (a pedal) down to the floor, especially to accelerate.

examples.text: our driver floored the pedal
I don't remember much about the flight from Chicago to Denver. We landed a little after eleven, and I ran through the airport, ran to my car. Floored it most of the way home.

glosses: To silence by a conclusive answer or retort.

examples.text: floor an opponent
Floored or crushed by him.

glosses: To amaze or greatly surprise.

examples.text: We were floored by his confession.

Some of the attendees were “absolutely floored,” said an official familiar with the proceedings. That someone in the U.S. government could “make an argument that is so nakedly against transparency, in light of the unfolding catastrophe, was…shocking and disturbing.”

glosses: To finish or make an end of.

examples.text: floor a college examination
I've floored my little-go work

glosses: To set a lower bound.

examples.text: floored division
